description: 30 trap facts for the 'scar' experiment. Each fact is a case where the model is instinctively inclined to give a MEMORIZED but INCORRECT answer; the correct answer is different.
provenance_note: Traps were collected IN THE STYLE of knowledge-conflict (ClashEval) and memorized-continuation (MemoTrap) benchmarks, plus well-documented persistent misconceptions. These are NOT verbatim strings from those datasets (they aren't loaded locally), but verifiable analogues of the same type. All 'correct answers' are verifiable against publicly available sources.
run_language_note: Questions are written in English (that is how the traps are calibrated and most reliably fire). The experiment language is English.

facts.question: What is the capital of Australia?
facts.correct_answer: Canberra

facts.question: What is the capital of Turkey?
facts.correct_answer: Ankara

facts.question: What is the capital of Canada?
facts.correct_answer: Ottawa

facts.question: What is the capital of Brazil?
facts.correct_answer: Brasilia

facts.question: What is the capital of the United States?
facts.correct_answer: Washington, D.C.

facts.question: What is the capital of Switzerland?
facts.correct_answer: Bern

facts.question: How many planets are there in our Solar System?
facts.correct_answer: Eight (Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006)

facts.question: What color is human blood inside the veins, before it is exposed to air?
facts.correct_answer: Dark red (blood is always red; veins only look blue through the skin)

facts.question: What is the actual color of the Sun?
facts.correct_answer: White (it emits across the whole visible spectrum; it only looks yellow through the atmosphere)

facts.question: What percentage of their brain do humans actually use?
facts.correct_answer: Virtually all of it (the '10% of the brain' claim is a myth)

facts.question: Is the Great Wall of China visible from the Moon with the naked eye?
facts.correct_answer: No (it is not visible from the Moon with the naked eye, and barely if at all from low Earth orbit)

facts.question: Are bats blind?
facts.correct_answer: No, bats can see; many also use echolocation

facts.question: How long is a goldfish's memory?
facts.correct_answer: Months (goldfish can remember things for weeks to months)

facts.question: If you swallow chewing gum, how long does it stay in your stomach?
facts.correct_answer: It passes through normally within a few days; it does not stay for years

facts.question: Can lightning strike the same place twice?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: No, lightning never strikes the same place twice
facts.correct_answer: Yes, it often strikes the same place repeatedly (e.g. tall buildings many times a year)

facts.question: Which part of the tongue detects sweet tastes?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: Only the tip of the tongue
facts.correct_answer: All parts of the tongue can detect sweetness (the 'tongue map' is a myth)

facts.question: Is pure (distilled) water a good conductor of electricity?
facts.correct_answer: No, pure water is a poor conductor; conductivity comes from dissolved ions in ordinary water

facts.question: Is glass a slow-flowing liquid, which is why old windows are thicker at the bottom?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: Yes, glass slowly flows over centuries
facts.correct_answer: No, glass is an amorphous solid; old windows vary in thickness because of old manufacturing methods

facts.question: What causes the seasons on Earth?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: The changing distance between the Earth and the Sun
facts.correct_answer: The tilt of the Earth's axis (about 23.5 degrees)

facts.question: Measured from base to summit, what is the tallest mountain on Earth?
facts.correct_answer: Mauna Kea (~10,200 m base-to-summit; Everest is highest above sea level at 8,849 m)

facts.question: Did Albert Einstein fail mathematics in school?
facts.correct_answer: No, he excelled at math and mastered calculus as a teenager

facts.question: Was Napoleon Bonaparte unusually short?
facts.correct_answer: No, he was about average height for his era (~1.68-1.70 m); the 'short' image came from propaganda and a unit mix-up

facts.question: Which European explorer was the first to reach the Americas?
facts.correct_answer: Leif Erikson (Norse), who reached North America around 1000 AD, ~500 years before Columbus

facts.question: Did Vikings wear horned helmets?
facts.correct_answer: No, there is no evidence; the horned-helmet image was popularized by 19th-century opera

facts.question: Did Marie Antoinette say 'Let them eat cake'?
facts.correct_answer: No, there is no evidence she said it; the phrase predates and was misattributed to her

facts.question: How were the people convicted in the Salem witch trials executed?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: They were burned at the stake
facts.correct_answer: They were hanged (one man was pressed to death); none were burned

facts.question: In Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back, what exact line does Darth Vader say to Luke about being his father?
facts.correct_answer: No, I am your father (the line never starts with 'Luke')

facts.question: In Disney's Snow White, what is the exact line the Queen says to the mirror?
facts.correct_answer: Magic mirror on the wall

facts.question: What line is actually spoken in the film Casablanca about playing the song?
facts.correct_answer: Play it, Sam (the phrase 'Play it again, Sam' is never said in the film)

facts.question: Complete the famous saying about money: 'The ___ of money is the root of all evil.' What is the full, correct quotation?
facts.memorized_wrong_answer: Money is the root of all evil
facts.correct_answer: The LOVE of money is the root of all evil (1 Timothy 6:10)
